paragraphs.title: A Call to Thank God for His Kindness

easy.explanation: Verse 1 begins, “O give thanks unto the LORD.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalm call people to give thanks?

easy.explanation: The phrase “his mercy endureth for ever” is repeated.
easy.q: What is said about the LORD's mercy?

answers: Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD
easy.explanation: The verses address Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD.
easy.q: Which groups are called to speak in verses 2–4?

answers: A call to thank God for His goodness and mercy
A description of going to war
medium.explanation: The passage repeatedly calls people to give thanks because God is good and His mercy endures forever.
medium.q: What is the main idea of verses 1–4?

answers: It moves from one person to one family only
It moves from Israel to every nation
It begins generally and then names Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD
medium.explanation: The psalm first gives a general call and then identifies three groups.
medium.q: How does the call to thanksgiving develop?

medium.explanation: Here “mercy” refers to God's enduring kindness and faithful love.
medium.q: In the KJV phrase “his mercy endureth for ever,” what does “mercy” most nearly mean?

answers: That mercy belongs only to Israel
challenge.explanation: The repeated words stress the permanence of God's mercy.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of “his mercy endureth for ever” emphasize?

answers: Verse 1 concerns enemies, while the others concern gates
Verse 1 gives a general call, while the others address specific groups
challenge.explanation: The first verse is general; the following verses name particular hearers.
challenge.q: What is the difference between verse 1 and verses 2–4?

challenge.explanation: Each verse ends with the same statement about God's enduring mercy.
challenge.q: Which phrase connects all four verses?

paragraphs.title: Deliverance from Distress and Trust in God

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “I called upon the LORD in distress.”
easy.q: From what situation did the psalmist call upon the LORD?

answers: Set him in a large place
easy.explanation: The LORD answered him and “set me in a large place.”
easy.q: What did the LORD do in response?

easy.explanation: The passage says it is better to trust in the LORD than in man or princes.
easy.q: In whom is it better to trust?

answers: Calling on the LORD led to an answer and relief
Calling on the LORD caused hiding
Calling on the LORD brought enemies
medium.explanation: The psalmist called in distress, and the LORD answered by giving him room.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between calling on the LORD and being in a large place?

answers: The LORD is the dependable source of help
medium.explanation: The verses contrast trust in God with dependence on human strength or rank.
medium.q: Why is trust in the LORD better than confidence in man or princes?

answers: A condition of trouble and pressure
medium.explanation: “Distress” means a difficult and pressing situation.

challenge.explanation: The psalmist begins in distress and ends by affirming trust in the LORD.
challenge.q: What emotional movement appears in verses 5–9?

answers: A movement from pressure to relief
A movement from wealth to poverty
A movement from the Temple to a house
challenge.explanation: The contrast portrays deliverance from confinement and trouble into freedom and relief.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between a “large place” and distress suggest?

answers: Both are presented as less reliable than trusting in the LORD
Only princes are described as helpers
challenge.explanation: The verses compare trust in God with confidence in ordinary people and rulers.
challenge.q: How do verses 8–9 distinguish between man and princes?

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “All nations compassed me about.”
The psalmist repeatedly says that he will act “in the name of the LORD.”
easy.q: In whose name does the psalmist face his enemies?
What happened when the psalmist was thrust toward falling?

answers: They enter the gates of righteousness
medium.explanation: The repeated language of being compassed about emphasizes their surrounding presence.
medium.q: What is repeated about the enemies in verses 10–12?

answers: The LORD's name leads to their defeat
medium.explanation: The psalmist repeats that in the LORD's name he will destroy or overcome them.
medium.q: What relationship is shown between trusting in the LORD's name and the enemies' fate?

medium.explanation: “Quenched” means extinguished, like a fire that goes out.
medium.q: In the comparison with bees and thorn fire, what does “quenched” mean?

answers: The feeling of being surrounded on every side
challenge.explanation: The repetition intensifies the sense of danger and pressure.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of “compassed me about” emphasize?

answers: Being thrust toward falling versus being helped by the LORD
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts the enemy's attempt to make him fall with the LORD's help.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in verse 13?

answers: It presents the LORD as the psalmist's strength and salvation
It describes only the enemies' weakness
It asks to enter the gate
challenge.explanation: The psalmist summarizes his deliverance by calling the LORD his strength, song, and salvation.
challenge.q: How does verse 14 relate to overcoming the enemies?

paragraphs.title: Voices of Joy, Strength, and Life

answers: The voice of rejoicing and salvation
easy.explanation: Verse 15 mentions “the voice of rejoicing and salvation.”
easy.q: What is heard in the tabernacles of the righteous?

easy.explanation: The passage repeatedly says that the right hand of the LORD “doeth valiantly.”
easy.q: How is the hand of the LORD described?

answers: To declare the works of the LORD
easy.explanation: Verse 17 says, “I shall not die, but live, and declare the works of the LORD.”
easy.q: Why does the psalmist say he will live?

medium.explanation: The righteous respond to salvation with rejoicing.
medium.q: What is the connection between salvation and rejoicing?

answers: The LORD chastened him but did not give him over to death
medium.explanation: The verse recognizes both discipline and preservation from death.
medium.q: What does the psalmist acknowledge in verse 18?

answers: Acts with strength and victorious power
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the LORD's hand as powerful and triumphant.
medium.q: What does “doeth valiantly” mean in this passage?

answers: Life gives the psalmist opportunity to tell what God has done
Life prevents him from giving thanks
Life is described as an enemy
challenge.explanation: The psalmist says he will live in order to declare the LORD's works.
challenge.q: How are life and declaring God's works connected?

answers: Joyful salvation alongside the memory of discipline
challenge.explanation: The passage celebrates salvation while also remembering chastening and danger.

answers: To emphasize God's active power and victory
To identify the number of enemies
challenge.explanation: The repetition highlights the LORD's powerful and successful action.
challenge.q: Why is “the right hand of the LORD” repeated?

paragraphs.title: The Gates of Righteousness and the Rejected Stone

easy.explanation: Verse 19 says, “Open to me the gates of righteousness.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask to have opened?
Who shall enter through the LORD's gate?

answers: It became the head stone of the corner
easy.explanation: Verse 22 says the rejected stone became the head stone of the corner.
easy.q: What happened to the stone rejected by the builders?

medium.explanation: He says, “I will go into them, and I will praise the LORD.”
medium.q: Why does the psalmist want to enter the gates of righteousness?

answers: What was central became a gate
medium.explanation: The stone refused by the builders became the chief or central stone.
medium.q: What reversal is shown in the image of the stone?

answers: A chief and important stone in a building
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a prominent stone with an important structural position.
medium.q: What does “the head stone of the corner” refer to?

answers: Both are images of acceptance and restoration through God's salvation
Both describe enemies surrounding the psalmist
challenge.explanation: Entering the gate and the stone's new position both portray deliverance and a restored place.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the gates of righteousness and the rejected stone?

challenge.explanation: Verse 23 says, “This is the LORD's doing.”
challenge.q: What is identified as the source of this remarkable reversal?

answers: The LORD's marvelous work leads to rejoicing in the day He made
The marvelous work leads to fear of enemies
challenge.explanation: After describing the LORD's marvelous work, the psalmist rejoices in the day the LORD made.
challenge.q: What connection exists between verses 23 and 24?

easy.explanation: He asks, “Save now” and “send now prosperity.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist request in verse 25?

answers: He that cometh in the name of the LORD
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the LORD.”

answers: With a call to thank the LORD for His mercy
With a request for the gates of righteousness
easy.explanation: The final verse repeats the call to give thanks because God's mercy endures forever.

answers: A request for salvation and prosperity
medium.explanation: After praising God, the psalmist asks for continued help and success.
medium.q: What follows the thanksgiving for deliverance?

answers: The LORD has shown them light
medium.explanation: The verse says, “God is the LORD, which hath shewed us light.”
medium.q: What do the people proclaim in verse 27?

medium.explanation: He says, “I will praise thee” and “I will exalt thee.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist do in verse 28?

answers: It repeats the call to thank God for His goodness and mercy
challenge.explanation: The psalm begins and ends with the same call to give thanks because the LORD is good and His mercy endures forever.
challenge.q: How does the final verse connect with the opening of the psalm?

answers: Petition, blessing, festival preparation, personal praise, and final thanksgiving
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from asking for help to blessing, worship, and concluding thanksgiving.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence in verses 25–29?

answers: The psalmist combines prayer for help with recognition of God's mercy
The psalmist focuses only on enemies
challenge.explanation: The passage includes both a request for salvation and grateful praise for God's goodness.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from petition to thanksgiving?
